reading.body:
High-Flyer is a Chinese quant fund that built its own AI training stack, which is the pattern to watch as compute becomes the constraint.

The company runs three things at once: a deep learning training platform called Firefly, a hedge fund that invests using AI, and basic science research. Firefly Two is described as scheduling training at the task level with second-scale response, so researchers share the machine rather than each holding a slice. The software layer named is a high-performance operator library, a distributed communication framework, and a file system built for AI development.

The hedge fund is the part that matters for AI scaling. Trading revenue is a way to pay for compute without selling model access, which is the usual route. A firm that funds its own training from capital markets has a different constraint than a lab that must raise or earn from products. The data does not say how large that compute is, where it sits, or what power it draws.

What the record does not cover is nearly everything about the physical side. There is no facility, no capacity, no chip count, no power contract, no location beyond a headquarters city. It also lists no products and no litigation. So the claim that High-Flyer is a compute story is supported only by the existence of a self-built training platform and a fund to pay for it, not by any measurement of either.

profile_text.body:
High-Flyer is a for-profit startup founded in 2015 and headquartered in Hangzhou, China. Its website describes the company as focused on frontier technology research and development, using AI to inspire creativity and imagination. It presents itself as three connected efforts: the Firefly (萤火) deep learning training platform, High-Flyer Quant, a hedge fund that uses AI for investing, and AI basic science research.

The site describes Firefly Two as built around task-level time-sharing, with a scheduling system that responds in seconds so that each researcher has a smooth training experience. It also lists a software layer: a high-performance operator library (hfai.nn), a distributed training communication framework (hfreduce), and 3FS, a large-capacity, high-bandwidth file system built for AI development. According to the company, these let AI models scale across multiple nodes for large-scale parallel training.

The available record contains no litigation involving the company.
